clue.text: Company doctor taking drug for deep depression

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A firm's medic is on drugs to treat severe clinical depression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deep depression' reads as a mental state, but it is a valley in the landscape.
explanation.definitionFit: A combe is a steep, narrow valley, a hollow in hillside terrain.

clue.text: Whatever the weather, heroic marine's on manoeuvres

indicators.note: military manoeuvres move troops about, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the possessive s is kept as a letter here

explanation.surface: A heroic marine is out on military exercises in all conditions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manoeuvres' rearranges HEROIC, MARINES and ON together.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom meaning regardless of circumstances, no matter what the conditions are.

clue.text: Note tiny Tim's end

parts.note: mini means very small

indicators.note: only the final letter of the name Tim is used

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: Write down the end of little Tim's story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Note' reads as jot down; it is a musical note.
explanation.definitionFit: A minim is a half note in music, worth two crotchets.

clue.text: Dubious rare pot — mistake in text

indicators.note: dubious means unreliable, so the letters of rare are rearranged

parts.note: a pot belly is a tum, informal for stomach

explanation.surface: A suspicious rare vase, but it is a misprint.
explanation.definitionFit: An erratum is an error in printing or writing, listed in a correction slip.

clue.text: Tucking into wine, no one goes back to old musical instrument

indicators.note: one piece tucks inside the word for the wine, so it is a container instruction

parts.note: claret is red Bordeaux wine

indicators.note: the words no and one are read from right to left

parts.note: taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone tucks into the wine while nobody turns back to an antique instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes back' reads the no-and-one pair as ION; the image of drinking wine hides the container instruction 'Tucking into'.
explanation.definitionFit: A clarionet is an old spelling and form of the clarinet, a woodwind used in early orchestras.

clue.text: Batter used in a sort of sandwich

definitions.meaning: to strike repeatedly, as with a cudgel
a triple-decker sandwich of toast, chicken and bacon

explanation.surface: Batter is put into a type of sandwich.
explanation.definitionFit: Beating with a heavy stick and a three-layer filled snack share one word.

clue.text: Poised for action with reference to the money

parts.note: at can mean in respect of, as in good at sums
the ready is slang for cash

explanation.surface: Prepared to act regarding finances.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for prepared and waiting, like a weapon held up and aimed.

clue.text: Implant after this month on the sick list

indicators.note: the sick-list word comes after the month abbreviation in the answer

parts.note: inst., instant, means of the current month in old business letters
someone on the sick list is ill

explanation.surface: Plant something after this month while off work sick.
explanation.definitionFit: To instil an idea is to fix it gradually in the mind, to plant it there.

clue.text: Census-taker loses his head and gets fractional dividend

indicators.note: the census-taker word drops its first letter

parts.note: an enumerator counts people for a census

explanation.surface: A census official is beheaded and receives a partial share payout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dividend' suggests money; it is the number divided in a fraction.
explanation.definitionFit: In a fraction the top figure is the quantity to be divided by the denominator.

clue.text: In a single journey, he should go through all the seasons

definitions.text: In a single journey, he should go through all the seasons

parts.words: In a single journey, he should go through all the seasons
parts.note: seasons are season tickets, and singles are one-way tickets, checked by a railway official on a train

explanation.surface: On one trip, he ought to pass through spring, summer, autumn and winter.
explanation.definitionFit: A rail official examines passengers' passes, singles and season tickets alike.

clue.text: Young person's outfit in clubs, perhaps

parts.note: a minor is someone below legal adult age
a suit is a set of matching clothes

explanation.surface: A child's clothes as worn in a golf or social club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clubs' looks like a place to wear an outfit; it is the card suit, one of the two lower-ranking suits in bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: In bridge, clubs and diamonds are the lesser-scoring card suits, below hearts and spades.

clue.text: Tree about to give endless delight, turning

indicators.note: the whole run of letters is read backwards

parts.note: C, short for circa, means about

indicators.note: the word for delight loses its final letter

parts.note: to amuse is to delight

explanation.surface: A tree is set to give delight without end as it turns in the wind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts AMUSE to AMUS; C + AMUS gives CAMUS, and 'turning' reads that backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Sumac is a shrub or small tree of the genus Rhus, grown for its red autumn foliage.

clue.text: Sort of control required in the middle of nowhere

definitions.meaning: a handset for operating a television from a distance
far from towns and people, isolated

explanation.surface: A kind of control needed out in the wilds.
explanation.definitionFit: Distant operation and isolated location are both senses of far-off, one technical and one geographical.

clue.text: Stock exercises needed by girl with almost excessive appetite

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercises
Di is a girl's name, short for Diana

indicators.note: the word for excessive appetite loses its last letter

parts.note: greed is an excessive desire for food or more

explanation.surface: Livestock needs workouts, given a girl with a near-gluttonous appetite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stock' looks like goods or cattle but means ancestry; 'almost' trims GREED to GREE.
explanation.definitionFit: Stock in the sense of lineage or line of descent, as in coming from good breeding.

clue.text: Mix bacon with endless muesli: it can be eaten

indicators.note: to mix is to stir together, so the letters are shuffled
muesli loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Combine bacon with an unending bowl of cereal; it is edible.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' takes I off MUESLI, and 'Mix' rearranges BACON + MUESL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something consumable is fit to be used up, as food is when eaten.

clue.text: Trouble at home with chest of drawers

parts.note: to be in is to be at home
a commode is an ornamental chest of drawers

explanation.surface: Domestic upset involving a piece of bedroom furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: To incommode is to inconvenience or bother someone, a formal verb for causing difficulty.

clue.text: Tell nice English models to get customers

indicators.note: to model is to shape, so these letters are reshaped

explanation.surface: Tell pleasant English models to attract buyers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'models' reshapes TELL NICE into CLIENTEL, and E for English finishes the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A business's clientele is its body of regular patrons and buyers.

clue.text: Some police excel at hitting with this

definitions.text: Some police excel at hitting with this

indicators.note: only part of the following words supplies the letters, a portion run across them

explanation.surface: Certain police officers are expert at striking people with a particular weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across excEL AT HItting; the whole clue also describes the weapon, as police in South Asia use it.
explanation.definitionFit: A lathi is a long bamboo stick, iron-bound, carried by Indian police as a baton.

clue.text: Dislike parking off platform

indicators.note: the letter for parking goes off, removed from the word for a platform

parts.note: a podium is a raised platform for a speaker
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: Someone resents having parking removed from a raised stage area.
explanation.definitionFit: Odium is general hatred or disgust, strong aversion felt by people towards someone.

clue.text: Labelling old vessel in Chinese dynasty

indicators.note: one word goes inside the other, as the vessel sits in the dynasty

parts.note: the Ming dynasty ruled China from 1368 to 1644
Noah's ark is the ancient boat in Genesis

explanation.surface: Tagging an antique Ming vase.
explanation.definitionFit: Marking items means putting tags or labels on them.

clue.text: Pretentiousness shown by poet's whiskers

parts.note: side is an old word for putting on airs, swagger
Robert Burns is the Scottish national poet

explanation.surface: A poet's facial hair reveals his conceit.
explanation.definitionFit: Sideburns are strips of hair grown down the cheeks in front of the ears, a kind of facial hair.

clue.text: Songbird is hunter's baby

definitions.meaning: a small seed-eating bird of the finch family
from the nursery rhyme Bye baby ___, daddy's gone a-hunting

explanation.surface: A singing bird is a hunter's infant.
explanation.walkthrough: The rhyme 'Bye baby Bunting, Daddy's gone a-hunting' is a traditional British lullaby.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a finch-like bird and the infant in a lullaby about a father out hunting.

clue.text: Symptoms of crime, say, initially disconcert capital city

indicators.note: the word for crime is heard, spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: a sin is a moral offence or wrongdoing

indicators.note: only the opening letter of disconcert is used

parts.note: Rome is the capital of Italy

explanation.surface: Signs of criminality first unsettle a capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of crime, say' tempts as a definition; 'say' makes SIN sound as SYN.
explanation.definitionFit: A syndrome is a set of signs occurring together that characterise a medical condition.

clue.text: Right of admission to a course

definitions.meaning: the privilege of being allowed in somewhere
a dish served at a meal, the main or the one before it

explanation.surface: The right to enter a course of study.
explanation.definitionFit: The French-derived word covers both access granted to a club or society and a dish at dinner.

clue.text: Arrest after an argument

definitions.meaning: to take someone into custody, informal police slang
a quarrel or clash between people

explanation.surface: Arrested following a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: Police slang for detaining a suspect and a noun for a quarrel share one phrase.

clue.text: A bit of glass in one's ear can cause discomfort

indicators.note: heard by the ear rather than seen, so it is the sound that counts

parts.note: a pane is a sheet of window glass

explanation.surface: A glass splinter lodged in the ear can hurt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in one's ear' reads as the location of the glass, but it means the word is heard.
explanation.definitionFit: Pain is physical suffering or hurt, a stronger form of unease.

clue.text: Ancient tribesmen had diamonds and nickel

parts.note: ice is slang for diamonds
Ni is the chemical symbol for nickel

explanation.surface: Old tribal warriors possessed gemstones and metal.
explanation.walkthrough: The ICENI were the British tribe led by Boudicca against the Romans.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iceni were a Celtic people of East Anglia in Roman-era Britain.

clue.text: She wrote about school teachers — it's hard to swallow

parts.note: Angela Brazil wrote popular schoolgirl stories in the early twentieth century
the NUT was the National Union of Teachers, a British union

explanation.surface: A school-story author writes about teachers, and it's hard to accept.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hard to swallow' suggests unbelievable; it is literal, a tough-shelled thing to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: This edible seed of a South American tree has a very tough shell, so it is hard to eat.

clue.text: Fresh and vital, but always envious

parts.note: ever means at all times
green, as in green with envy, means jealous

explanation.surface: Lively and young, yet perpetually jealous.
explanation.definitionFit: Something perennially popular stays young and lively, never going stale.

clue.text: Nasty princess the Italian left (and won't be coming back)

definitions.note: a verb phrase standing for a noun: one who will not return

indicators.note: the Italian article departs, removed from the princess's name

parts.note: Goneril is King Lear's cruel eldest daughter in Shakespeare
il is the Italian for the

explanation.surface: A wicked princess, the Italian one, has gone away for good.
explanation.definitionFit: A goner is someone doomed or lost, who will not return or survive.
